In [[Greek mythology]], '''Aethusa''' ({{Langx|grc|Αἵθουσα|4=to light up', 'to burn', or 'radiant/ shining}}) was a daughter of [[Poseidon]] and the [[Pleiades (Greek mythology)|Pleiad]] [[Alcyone (Pleiad)|Alcyone]], daughter of [[Atlas (mythology)|Atlas]].<ref>[[Suda|Suida]], s.v. ''[https://topostext.org/work.php?work_id=240#omi.251 Homer]; [https://www.gutenberg.org/files/348/348-h/348-h.htm#link2H_4_0021 Of the Origin of Homer and Hesiod and their Contest, Fragment]'' 1.314</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Bell|first=Robert E.|title=Women of Classical Mythology: A Biographical Dictionary|publisher=ABC-CLIO|year=1991|isbn=9780874365818|pages=13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=[[Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology]]|last=Schmitz|first=Leonhard|year=1870|editor-last=Smith|editor-first=William|volume=1|place=Boston, MA|pages=51|contribution=Aethusa|contribution-url=http://www.ancientlibrary.com/smith-bio/0060.html|access-date=2007-11-04|archive-date=2010-06-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100608005629/http://www.ancientlibrary.com/smith-bio/0060.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was loved by [[Apollo]] and bore to him [[Eleuther]]<ref>[[Bibliotheca (Pseudo-Apollodorus)|Apollodorus]], 3.10.1; [[Pausanias (geographer)|Pausanias]], 9.20.2</ref> and [[Linus of Thrace|Linus]].<ref>Suida, s.v. ''[https://topostext.org/work.php?work_id=240#omi.251 Homer]; Of the Origin of Homer and Hesiod and their Contest, Fragment'' 1.314</ref> Through either of the latter two, Aethusa became the grandmother of [[Pierus of Emathia|Pierus]], father of [[Oeagrus]], father of the musician [[Orpheus]]. Because of this genealogical fact, she was usually identified as a [[Thracians|Thracian]].<ref name=":0">Suida, s.v. ''[https://topostext.org/work.php?work_id=240#omi.251 Homer]''</ref>

The word ''aethusa'' was used as an epithet for a [[portico]] that was open to the sun above.<ref>{{cite book | last = Jebb  | first = Richard Claverhouse  | authorlink = Richard Claverhouse Jebb  | title = Homer: An Introduction to the Iliad and the Odyssey  | publisher = James Maclehose and Sons  | year = 1887  | location = Glasgow  | url = https://archive.org/details/homeranintroduc00jebbgoog | page = [https://archive.org/details/homeranintroduc00jebbgoog/page/n74 58]  | quote = aethusa.  }}</ref>

According to [[Pliny the Elder|Pliny's]] ''[[Natural History (Pliny)|Naturalis Historia]]'', ''Aethusa'' is also the eponym of the Italian island which is now called [[Linosa]].
